context: EsDashboard is an internet-facing web application that provides an Elasticsearch-based dashboard for monitoring and visualizing Checkov security compliance failures within Azure DevOps (ADO) pipelines. The system serves Singapore region with Level 2 business criticality, enabling DevOps teams to track, analyze, and remediate infrastructure security violations detected during CI/CD processes.

userStories.title: View Checkov Failure Dashboard
userStories.iWantTo: view a comprehensive dashboard showing all Checkov failures across ADO pipelines
userStories.soThat: I can quickly identify and prioritize security compliance issues in our infrastructure deployments

acceptanceCriteria.given: I am an authenticated DevOps Engineer
acceptanceCriteria.when: I access the EsDashboard main page
acceptanceCriteria.then: I should see a dashboard with Checkov failure metrics, charts, and recent alerts

acceptanceCriteria.given: There are Checkov failures in the last 24 hours
acceptanceCriteria.then: I should see real-time failure counts, severity distribution, and affected pipelines

acceptanceCriteria.when: I click on a failure metric
acceptanceCriteria.then: I should be able to drill down to see detailed failure information

userStories.title: Filter and Search Failures
userStories.iWantTo: filter and search Checkov failures by pipeline, severity, time range, and failure type
userStories.soThat: I can focus on specific security issues that require immediate attention

acceptanceCriteria.given: I am viewing the failures list
acceptanceCriteria.when: I apply filters for severity level 'High' and time range 'Last 7 days'
acceptanceCriteria.then: I should see only high-severity failures from the past week

acceptanceCriteria.given: I am on the search interface
acceptanceCriteria.when: I search for a specific pipeline name or failure type
acceptanceCriteria.then: I should get filtered results matching my search criteria

userStories.title: View Detailed Failure Information
userStories.iWantTo: view detailed information about specific Checkov failures including code location, rule violated, and remediation suggestions
userStories.soThat: I can understand the issue and fix it efficiently

acceptanceCriteria.given: I click on a specific Checkov failure
acceptanceCriteria.then: I should see the violated security rule, affected code snippet, severity level, and recommended fix

acceptanceCriteria.when: I look at the remediation section
acceptanceCriteria.then: I should see actionable steps to resolve the security issue

userStories.title: Configure Data Ingestion from ADO
userStories.iWantTo: configure the system to automatically ingest Checkov failure data from ADO pipelines
userStories.soThat: the dashboard displays up-to-date failure information without manual intervention

acceptanceCriteria.given: I have ADO pipeline credentials and endpoints
acceptanceCriteria.when: I configure the data ingestion settings
acceptanceCriteria.then: the system should automatically fetch Checkov failure data every 15 minutes

acceptanceCriteria.given: A new Checkov failure occurs in an ADO pipeline
acceptanceCriteria.then: the failure should appear in the dashboard within 15 minutes

acceptanceCriteria.given: The ADO service is temporarily unavailable
acceptanceCriteria.when: the ingestion process encounters an error
acceptanceCriteria.then: the system should retry and log the failure for monitoring

userStories.title: Set Up Alerting and Notifications
userStories.iWantTo: configure alerts for critical Checkov failures and receive notifications
userStories.soThat: I can respond quickly to high-severity security issues

acceptanceCriteria.when: I set up a rule for critical severity failures
acceptanceCriteria.then: I should receive email notifications when critical failures occur

acceptanceCriteria.given: A critical Checkov failure is detected
acceptanceCriteria.then: relevant team members should receive notifications within 5 minutes

functionalRequirements.title: Dashboard Visualization System
functionalRequirements.description: The system must provide a web-based dashboard that displays Checkov failure metrics in real-time using charts, graphs, and tabular data visualization.
functionalRequirements.inputs: Elasticsearch data containing Checkov failure records
functionalRequirements.triggers: User accessing dashboard, automatic data refresh
functionalRequirements.mainFlow: Fetch data from Elasticsearch, process metrics, render visualizations
functionalRequirements.outputs: Interactive dashboard with charts, metrics, and failure lists

functionalRequirements.title: Advanced Search and Filtering
functionalRequirements.description: The system must provide comprehensive search and filtering capabilities allowing users to query Checkov failures by multiple criteria including pipeline, severity, time range, and failure type.
functionalRequirements.inputs: User search queries and filter parameters
functionalRequirements.triggers: User initiating search or applying filters
functionalRequirements.mainFlow: Parse search query, build Elasticsearch query, execute search, return filtered results
functionalRequirements.outputs: Filtered list of Checkov failures matching search criteria

functionalRequirements.title: Failure Detail Viewer
functionalRequirements.description: The system must display detailed information for individual Checkov failures including rule violations, code context, severity assessment, and remediation guidance.
functionalRequirements.triggers: User clicking on specific failure entry
functionalRequirements.mainFlow: Retrieve failure details from Elasticsearch, format data, display comprehensive view
functionalRequirements.outputs: Detailed failure view with code snippets, rules, and remediation steps

functionalRequirements.title: ADO Pipeline Integration
functionalRequirements.description: The system must automatically ingest Checkov failure data from Azure DevOps pipelines through REST API integration with configurable polling intervals.
functionalRequirements.inputs: ADO API endpoints, authentication credentials, pipeline identifiers
functionalRequirements.triggers: Scheduled polling, webhook notifications from ADO
functionalRequirements.mainFlow: Authenticate with ADO, fetch pipeline data, extract Checkov results, transform and store in Elasticsearch
functionalRequirements.outputs: Checkov failure data stored in Elasticsearch with proper indexing

functionalRequirements.title: Alert and Notification System
functionalRequirements.description: The system must provide configurable alerting for critical Checkov failures with multiple notification channels including email and integration with external monitoring systems.
functionalRequirements.inputs: Alert rules configuration, failure severity thresholds, notification preferences
functionalRequirements.mainFlow: Evaluate failure against alert rules, trigger notifications, log alert history
functionalRequirements.outputs: Email notifications, webhook calls, alert logs

errorAndEdgeCases: ADO API rate limiting and quota exhaustion
Elasticsearch cluster unavailability or performance degradation
Network timeouts during ADO data ingestion
Invalid or malformed Checkov failure data from ADO
Dashboard timeout with large datasets (>10k failures)
Concurrent user access causing resource contention
Missing or incomplete Checkov scan results
Duplicate failure records from multiple pipeline runs
Data retention policy conflicts with long-term trend analysis
assumptions: ADO pipelines have Checkov scanning enabled and configured
Elasticsearch cluster has sufficient storage and compute capacity
Network connectivity between EsDashboard and ADO is stable
Users have appropriate ADO permissions to access pipeline data
Checkov failure data format remains consistent across pipeline versions
Singapore region deployment meets data residency requirements
Internet-facing deployment includes appropriate security controls
Level 2 business criticality allows for planned maintenance windows
openQuestions: What are the specific data retention requirements for Checkov failure history?
Should the system integrate with existing SIEM or security orchestration platforms?
What are the expected concurrent user limits and performance SLAs?
Are there specific compliance standards (SOX, PCI DSS) that need to be addressed?
Should the system support role-based access control for different failure types?
What backup and disaster recovery requirements exist for the dashboard?
Should historical trend analysis include predictive analytics capabilities?
What integration points are needed with existing ADO work item tracking?

traceability.notes: Dashboard visualization directly supports user story for viewing Checkov failures with interactive metrics
Advanced search functionality enables security analysts to filter and focus on specific failure types
Detailed failure viewer provides comprehensive information needed for issue resolution
ADO integration requirement supports automated data ingestion with error handling
Alerting system enables proactive response to critical security failures

tasks: Develop responsive design for mobile access
Develop export functionality for failure details
Develop error handling and retry logic

definitionOfDone: Code reviewed and approved by at least two team members
Unit tests written with minimum 80% code coverage
Integration tests passing for all API endpoints
Security scan completed with no critical vulnerabilities
Performance testing meets SLA requirements (sub-3 second response)
Documentation updated including API specs and user guides
Cross-browser compatibility tested (Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge)
Deployment pipeline validated in staging environment
Monitoring and alerting configured for production readiness
sprintPlanning: Sprint 1: Core dashboard infrastructure and basic Elasticsearch integration
Sprint 2: ADO pipeline data ingestion and basic failure visualization
Sprint 3: Advanced search and filtering capabilities
Sprint 4: Detailed failure viewer and remediation guidance
Sprint 5: Alert system and notification framework
Sprint 6: Performance optimization and security hardening
Sprint 7: User acceptance testing and production deployment
Each sprint should include dedicated time for security review and compliance validation
